job.title: Wellbeing Practitioner
job.description:
Do work that truly matters — with professional depth and real impact.
  
This organisation is expanding its Veteran Services team and is seeking experienced Wellbeing Practitioners to deliver trauma-informed, strengths-based case management to veterans and their families with complex needs.
  
This is a professionally governed role involving psychosocial assessment, care coordination, ethical decision-making, and evidence-based practice. You will work within structured frameworks to support clients to navigate complex health and social systems, build wellbeing, and achieve sustainable outcomes.
  
The Opportunity
As a Wellbeing Practitioner, you will deliver short- and long-term case management interventions, including psychosocial assessment, individualised care planning, health literacy development, and access to financial and emergency supports. You will work collaboratively with internal teams and external partners to ensure coordinated, veteran-centred care.
  
Key Responsibilities
• Conduct holistic psychosocial assessments and develop individualised case management plans
• Deliver trauma-informed, strengths-based, person-centred case management
• Manage an active caseload of approximately 15–20 clients based on complexity and need
• Coordinate referrals across health, mental health, housing, financial and community services
• Support access to emergency relief, applications for assistance and other wellbeing support packages
• Promote health literacy and guide clients through complex service systems
• Identify, manage and escalate risk and high-complexity cases appropriately
• Maintain accurate, timely and confidential case notes and documentation within CRM systems
• Build strong collaborative relationships with partners including DVA, Open Arms, health providers, housing services and community organisations
• Participate in supervision, peer reviews, team meetings and professional development activities
  
The Cohort
You will support veterans who may be experiencing mental health challenges, social isolation, financial stress, transition from institutional settings, or the impacts of trauma and complex life stressors. This is meaningful, complex work requiring sound professional judgement, emotional resilience, and strong ethical boundaries.
  
What We’re Looking For
  
Essential:
• Degree in Human Services, Health Sciences, Social Work, Psychology or equivalent enabling eligibility for professional membership/registration (e.g. AASW, AHPRA, PACFA)
• Minimum 2 years’ experience in a similar case management, wellbeing or psychosocial support role
• Strong experience in strengths-based and trauma-informed practice
• Ability to conduct psychosocial assessments and develop structured care plans
• High-level written and verbal communication skills and strong attention to detail
• Ability to work autonomously within governance, ethical and practice frameworks
• Willingness to undertake relevant advocacy or practice framework training
• Current driver’s licence
  
Highly Regarded:
• Experience working with veterans, Defence, or complex trauma cohorts
• Knowledge of health, mental health, and social service systems
• Strong clinical reasoning, ethical decision-making and risk management capability
  
What’s On Offer
• Competitive salary + super + salary packaging
• Performance-based incentive opportunities
• Potential Part-time work depending on availability 
• Structured supervision, reflective practice and professional development
• Career progression within a growing, purpose-driven organisation
• The opportunity to do impactful, evidence-based work that genuinely changes lives
  
If you’re a qualified, values-driven practitioner who wants to do meaningful, professionally supported work with real-world impact, we’d love to hear from you.

About the Role

This is your opportunity to take ownership of a significant operational portfolio leading on-road assessing and building repair relationships to drive performance, accountability, and continuous improvement within one of Australia’s most respected and fastest-growing insurance groups.

You will lead a team of ~20 home assessors and 3-4 team leaders, championing a culture of excellence, proactive decision-making, and technical integrity across geographically dispersed operations.

This role is pivotal in delivering strategic uplift within a high-volume, customer-facing environment — improving claim life cycles, strengthening leadership capability, and resetting what “good” and “great” look like across the function.

You'll provide clear direction, coaching and development to your team — ensuring every member understands their role, owns their accountability and has the skills to deliver against business objectives.

Key Accountabilities

Be directly responsible for leading, coaching and developing the Onroad Home Assessing Team, driving high performance against KPIs, service standards and compliance requirements
  • Act as key liaison for internal and external stakeholders, collaborating across the end-to-end Home value chain to deliver against overall business objectives
  • Work closely with the Commercial Manager to vet, procure and govern supplier services within appropriate contractual and compliance frameworks
  • Monitor, audit and manage supplier performance nationally, ensuring adequate capacity, coverage and adherence to procurement protocols and best practice standards
  • Act as escalation point for complex negotiations and high-profile disputes, working closely with the Claims Operations Team
  • Identify and report on key trends, risks and opportunities within the Home Assessing & Supply team and broader Building Repair industry
  • Lead the team through Change Programs while maintaining strong knowledge of market developments, regulatory requirements, systems and products
About You
  • Extensive management experience, including leading teams & having accountability of business results, minimum of 5 years preferred
  • Strong knowledge of the Home Assessing, Building Repair & Restoration environment and associated market practices and standards
  • Strong commercial acumen and proven capability in the development and execution of strategic programs of work
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to communicate with stakeholders of all levels, along with accurate report writing  

What's In It for you?
  • Competitive salary package (including vehicle/phone etc).
  • Operate with autonomy and influence in a major national insurer undergoing transformational growth.
  • Grow and lead a talented, technically strong team with visible impact on business performance.
  • Be part of a collaborative leadership group with regular interaction across states.

Based from the Sunshine office, the role requires a strong on-site presence (approximately 80%) to drive cultural alignment and team connection.  Flexibility will increase over time once stability and performance are achieved. Occasional interstate travel is expected.

job.title: Environmental Business Partner - Qld
job.description:
Are you an experienced environmental professional who enjoys getting out on site, solving practical challenges and working alongside operational leaders to make a genuine difference?

Our client is Australia's largest vertically integrated construction materials company, and today they are seeking an experienced Environment Business Partner to support their extensive Queensland operations.

This is an opportunity to combine your technical environmental expertise with a highly visible, operationally focused business partnering role, influencing environmental compliance, risk management and continuous improvement across a diverse network of quarries, concrete batching plants, asphalt operations and recycling facilities.

Reporting to the Senior Environment Business Partner, you will work closely with Quarry Managers, Regional Managers and operational teams, providing practical advice, coaching and guidance to strengthen environmental capability and accountability.
 
This is not a desk-based compliance role.  Success will come from your ability to establish credibility on site, understand operational challenges and translate environmental obligations into practical solutions that support both compliance and business performance.
 
Your key responsibilities will include:
  • Partner with operational leaders to strengthen environmental compliance, risk management and site performance.
  • Conduct site inspections, environmental audits and assurance activities, identifying risks and improvement opportunities.
  • Provide practical advice on environmental approvals, licence conditions, legislation and operational requirements.
  • Support environmental monitoring programs, including water, dust, noise, emissions and other site-specific obligations.
  • Coordinate environmental compliance reporting, including annual returns, monitoring results and National Pollutant Inventory (NPI) submissions.
  • Investigate environmental incidents and complaints, identify root causes and support corrective actions.
  • Review environmental management plans, approvals and operating conditions to maintain compliance.
  • Advise operational teams on land disturbance, vegetation clearing, water management and other site activities.
  • Coach and educate site personnel, building environmental capability, ownership and accountability.
  • Work with consultants, regulators and internal stakeholders to resolve environmental matters and support continuous improvement.
  • Contribute to environmental improvement initiatives and the implementation of Boral's broader environmental strategy.
What you will bring to this role:
  • You will be a technically capable environmental professional with the confidence, initiative and interpersonal skills to influence outcomes in a complex operational environment.
  • A relevant tertiary qualification in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Management or a related discipline.
  • Approximately five years or more of environmental experience within heavy industry, mining, quarrying, construction, manufacturing, waste management or a regulatory environment.
  • Strong working knowledge of environmental legislation, approvals, licence conditions and compliance requirements.
  • Practical experience with environmental monitoring, inspections, incident investigations, reporting and risk management.
  • The ability to interpret technical and regulatory requirements and translate them into practical operational solutions.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with the confidence to advise, coach and influence site and regional management teams.
  • A proactive, self-directed approach, with the ability to prioritise competing activities across multiple locations.
  • Sound commercial judgement and an appreciation of the need to balance environmental compliance with operational realities.
  • Experience working across multiple operational sites, particularly within quarrying, mining or other extractive industries, will be highly regarded.
  • Exposure to environmental regulator engagement, approvals or licence variations would also be advantageous.
  • Importantly, you will enjoy being visible in the business, building trusted relationships and taking ownership of delivering outcomes.
Why Join this Icon - So what's in it for you?

This is an opportunity to make a meaningful contribution within an established Australian organisation where environmental performance is integral to business operations.

You'll benefit from:
  • Competitive remuneration
  • Variety and autonomy: A diverse portfolio of operational sites presenting interesting technical and environmental challenges.
  • Genuine business influence: Work directly with operational decision-makers, helping shape practical environmental outcomes.
  • Field-based engagement: A balanced mix of site visits, operational collaboration and office-based technical work.
  • Professional development: Broaden your exposure across quarrying, construction materials, manufacturing and recycling operations.
  • Supportive leadership: Work alongside an experienced Senior Environment Business Partner who values initiative, collaboration and getting things done.
  • Long-term opportunity: Join a major Australian business with an extensive operational footprint and ongoing environmental improvement priorities.
Location and Travel
Based in Milton, Brisbane, this role requires regular travel across Queensland to support operational sites.
During the initial three to six months, approximately two nights away from home per week may be required as you develop your understanding of the business, build relationships and become familiar with site operations.
Flexibility is available to work from operational locations where appropriate.

job.description:

This is a genuine new-business role for someone who enjoys building relationships, creating opportunities and taking ownership of their market.

  • Resilience and a results-focused mindset
  • Willingness to learn and work within a proven sales process

The environment
This is a role for someone who enjoys being out in the market rather than sitting behind a desk all day.

You’ll spend your time meeting customers, building relationships, developing opportunities and growing your network.

Our client offers genuine autonomy, supported by a comprehensive induction, product training and a structured approach to helping new starters build confidence and momentum.

The Brisbane market offers significant growth potential, with a broad range of industries and customers still available to develop.

job.description:
REGIONAL OPERATIONS MANAGER – QUARRIES

* Lead nine quarry operations across a large and diverse regional portfolio
* Take ownership of an approximately $95 million P&L and two million tonnes of annual sales
* Deliver significant operational, asset, resource development and capital priorities


Your next opportunity!
This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished quarrying leader to take responsibility for a significant regional portfolio within one of Australia’s leading construction materials organisations.

Reporting directly to the General Manager, you will lead nine quarry operations across Queensland and the Northern Territory, supported by experienced Quarry Managers and specialist leaders across assets, logistics, finance, commercial, property, sales and safety.

With an approximately $95 million P&L, annual sales of around two million tonnes and a substantial program of operational and capital investment, you will have genuine scope to shape performance, strengthen operational consistency and deliver lasting improvement across a diverse and commercially important portfolio.

The Opportunity
Your portfolio includes operations across Cairns, Townsville, Mackay, Wide Bay, Toowoomba and Darwin.
The role may be based in Brisbane, Townsville or another practical Queensland location, with Mackay, Cairns and the Wide Bay-Burnett region also open for consideration. Regular travel across the portfolio will be required.

You will lead a group of Quarry Managers with varying levels of operational, commercial and leadership experience. Your role will be to establish credibility quickly, create a consistent operating cadence and ensure each site receives the right level of leadership, challenge and support.

Key priorities will include:
· Securing the long-term continuity of quarry resources and raw materials
· Improving fixed-plant productivity, reliability and cost-per-unit performance
· Delivering significant operational and capital projects
· Establishing consistent KPIs, operating metrics and performance disciplines
· Strengthening accountability and capability across the Quarry Manager group
· Implementing and embedding key quarry safety initiatives
· Maintaining safe, compliant and environmentally responsible operations

Planned and potential investment includes a new primary crushing circuit, significant fixed-plant development, sand quarry asset replacement and a range of resource development, stripping, mobile equipment and site infrastructure projects.

Your Responsibilities
You will be accountable for:
· Providing operational leadership across nine quarrying operations
· Leading, coaching and developing the portfolio’s Quarry Managers
· Managing an approximately $95 million regional P&L
· Delivering production, safety, cost, margin and operational performance outcomes
· Driving fixed-plant and mobile-equipment optimisation
· Developing business cases and leading operational input into capital projects
· Identifying and prioritising replacement, continuity and growth investment
· Ensuring long-term resource availability and operational continuity
· Building greater consistency and standardisation across the regional network
· Partnering with finance, commercial, assets, logistics, property, sales and safety teams
· Managing relationships with regulators, councils, communities and other stakeholders
· Maintaining strong site visibility through regular regional travel

What you will bring
This role requires more than broad heavy-industry leadership. You will need the technical and operational credibility to engage experienced Quarry Managers, understand what is happening beneath the headline numbers and challenge performance constructively.
You will bring:
· An open Site Senior Executive (SSE) qualification, or the background and capability to obtain the required Queensland qualification quickly
· Substantial operational leadership experience within quarrying, aggregates or a closely aligned environment
· Previous responsibility for a large quarry or multiple quarry operations
· A deep understanding of safe, productive and commercially successful quarry operations
· Strong financial literacy and previous accountability for operational P&Ls, budgets and forecasts
· Experience developing capital business cases and delivering complex operational or asset projects
· Knowledge of fixed-plant optimisation, crushing operations, mobile equipment and resource development
· Demonstrated success leading experienced operational managers across multiple locations
· Strong knowledge of quarry safety, environmental and regulatory requirements
· The ability to interpret operational and financial data and turn it into decisive action
· A proactive leadership style and the confidence to take ownership without waiting for direction
· The flexibility to travel regularly across Queensland and the Northern Territory

Applicants from mining or mineral-processing environments may be considered where they can demonstrate highly transferable quarrying knowledge. However, direct experience within quarries, sand or aggregates will be strongly preferred.

Why join?
This is a rare opportunity to lead a quarrying portfolio with genuine scale, complexity and organisational visibility.

You will have significant autonomy, direct access to the General Manager and the opportunity to influence substantial operational and capital investment. You will also be supported by an established team of specialists across finance, assets, logistics, commercial, property and safety.

The organisation is seeking a leader who can move confidently between portfolio strategy and site-level operations, someone who knows when to step into the detail, when to challenge and when to empower others.

If you combine deep quarrying knowledge with commercial discipline, authentic leadership and the ability to turn priorities into action, we would welcome a confidential discussion.

job.description:
Project Manager – Major Concrete Operations
Sunshine Coast
Highly competitive Salary – paid relocation costs considered
  
Take ownership of the concrete operations supporting one of the Sunshine Coast’s most significant infrastructure projects and help establish the next operation from the ground up.
Our client is one of Australia’s leading construction materials organisations, with an extensive network of concrete, quarry and operational sites across the country and their people and products support major residential, commercial and civil infrastructure projects, helping to build stronger and more sustainable communities.
Based near Cooroy, you will lead the onsite concrete operations supporting a complex dam improvement project. You will manage plant performance, people, customer relationships, budgets and production delivery, while also helping prepare for an additional project operation at Coolum.
This is not a desk-based project-management position. You will be visible on site, working alongside your team, resolving operational issues and ensuring concrete is produced safely, consistently and in line with demanding project schedules.
This is a permanent position offering exposure to a strong pipeline of major projects beyond the current program.

Your next opportunity
Reporting to the Major Projects Manager for South East Queensland Concrete, you will initially take responsibility for an established onsite operation at Lake Macdonald.

As the project develops, you will also play an important role in establishing and staffing the next concrete operation at Coolum, with the potential to oversee multiple project sites across the Sunshine Coast.

You will lead four direct reports and coordinate approximately 10–15 drivers, working closely with the principal construction contractor, technical teams, suppliers and internal stakeholders.

The environment is fast-moving and highly accountable. Production volumes are significant, customer expectations are high and reliable plant performance is critical to the successful delivery of the broader infrastructure program.
  
Your responsibilities
  • Lead safe, reliable and efficient concrete operations across major project sites
  • Manage daily production requirements against changing project schedules and customer demand
  • Coordinate concrete orders, batching activities, testing and technical support
  • Maintain plant availability and coordinate preventative and reactive maintenance
  • Lead, coach and develop production employees and drivers
  • Create an engaged, accountable and safety-focused site culture
  • Conduct toolbox talks and ensure employees and contractors follow site requirements
  • Build strong working relationships with construction partners, engineers and other stakeholders
  • Respond quickly and professionally to customer concerns and operational issues
  • Manage site expenditure, labour costs, budgets, forecasts and operational performance
  • Monitor production, service, safety and plant-performance targets
  • Drive continuous improvement across plant operations, systems and processes
  • Support recruitment, onboarding and workforce planning for the new project operation
  • Assist with concrete batching and front-end loader operations when required
  • Ensure compliance with all safety, environmental and quality requirements
  
About you
You are an experienced operational leader who is equally comfortable talking with production employees on the plant floor and meeting with engineers and senior project stakeholders.
You remain calm under pressure, communicate clearly and take ownership when production priorities change or problems arise. You understand that strong customer relationships must be supported by safe operations, reliable equipment and consistent delivery.
You will ideally bring:
  • Operational leadership experience within concrete production or a closely related environment
  • A sound understanding of concrete batching, production processes and quality requirements
  • Experience leading plant-based teams in a safety-critical environment
  • Strong customer and stakeholder-management capability
  • The confidence to work directly with construction managers, engineers and project representatives
  • Experience managing production schedules, labour, costs, budgets and operational targets

If you are ready to take ownership of a complex concrete operation, build trusted customer relationships and lead a team delivering an important Sunshine Coast infrastructure project, we would like to hear from you.

job.title: Project Lead (Electrical) Engineer, Marulan Infrastructure Upgrade
job.description:
Project Lead Electrical Engineer $109.6M Major Infrastructure Upgrade | 
An exceptional opportunity exists for an experienced Project Lead Electrical Engineer to take technical ownership of the electrical, instrumentation and control systems behind a major $109.6 million mine infrastructure upgrade in the NSW Southern Highlands.

Hinchen Recruitment Group is partnering with one of Australia's largest vertically integrated construction materials company, to appoint a highly
capable electrical engineering leader to its Marulan Infrastructure Upgrade.

This is far more than a conventional engineering position. You'll be instrumental in delivering critical high-voltage power infrastructure, modern electrical distribution and sophisticated control systems, from engineering design through installation, safe  energisation, commissioning and operational handover.

If you enjoy solving complex engineering challenges, influencing major technical decisions and seeing your work come to life on site, this could be the opportunity you've been waiting for.

The project – engineering for the next generation, our client is undertaking a significant infrastructure investment at its mine, a strategically important operation supplying the other key businesses within their portfolio.

The approximately $109.6 million upgrade, with a 30-month delivery programme, includes:
  • Replacement of a primary crusher that has operated for close to 100 years.
  • Installation of a new impact crusher and associated materials handling infrastructure.
  • New stacker reclaimer and conveying systems.
  • Major high-voltage electrical infrastructure upgrades and power supply realignment.
  • New substations, transformers, switchrooms and motor control centres.
  • Integration of PLC, SCADA, instrumentation and automated control systems.
  • Rail realignment and supporting site infrastructure.
All of this will be delivered within an operating mine, where maintaining production, managing electrical risk and coordinating complex interfaces will be essential.
The opportunity – take the lead Reporting directly to the Project Director, you'll be the single point of technical accountability for the electrical, instrumentation and control engineering scope.
You'll lead a dedicated electrical team, work closely with mechanical and civil engineering leads, and engage with specialist contractors, equipment vendors, network service providers and operational stakeholders.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Taking ownership of electrical design assurance, technical integrity and engineering deliverables.
  • Leading high-voltage infrastructure works, including power supply realignment, substations, transformers and switchgear.
  • Overseeing switchrooms, motor control centres, variable speed drives, cabling, protection systems and electrical distribution.
  • Ensuring PLC, SCADA and instrumentation systems integrate effectively with existing operational infrastructure.
  • Managing electrical equipment specifications, technical tender evaluations, procurement support and vendor performance.
  • Leading electrical installation oversight, contractor coordination and quality assurance.
  • Planning and coordinating outages, electrical isolation, testing and staged energisation while minimising operational disruption.
  • Driving electrical completions, commissioning, functional testing and operational handover.
  • Providing visible safety leadership and ensuring compliance with relevant Australian Standards and NSW mine electrical safety requirements.
This is a role where your engineering judgement will matter. You'll be trusted to challenge designs, influence technical solutions, manage critical interfaces and deliver electrical infrastructure that is safe, reliable and fit for purpose.
About you – technically strong, commercially aware and delivery focused We're looking for an accomplished electrical engineering professional who brings both technical depth and practical major-project delivery experience.
You'll ideally offer:
  • A degree in Electrical Engineering.
  • A minimum of 10 years' electrical engineering experience within resources, mining, quarrying, cement or heavy industrial capital projects.
  • Previous experience leading the electrical discipline on a major engineering or infrastructure project.
  • Demonstrated delivery of high-voltage infrastructure, including substations, transformers and switchgear, from design through to energisation.
  • Experience with electrical and control systems supporting crushing, screening, conveying or comparable bulk materials handling operations.
  • Strong knowledge of protection coordination, arc flash assessment, earthing design, motor control centres, variable speed drives and AS/NZS 3000.
  • Practical experience with PLC and SCADA systems and their integration into existing industrial operations.
  • Proven site-based construction supervision experience in live, brownfield environments, including outage planning and staged commissioning.
  • The ability to lead technical teams, manage specialist contractors and work collaboratively across engineering disciplines.
Experience within cement, lime or quarry operations, network power supply upgrades, functional safety or safety instrumented systems would be highly regarded.
Above all, you'll be a confident engineering leader who combines technical credibility with practical judgement, strong safety values and a genuine commitment to successful project delivery.

Why this opportunity deserves your attention

A genuinely significant project: Be part of a $109.6 million infrastructure investment that will modernise a critical Australian industrial operation.
True engineering ownership: Take responsibility for the electrical discipline, with influence across engineering design, procurement, construction and commissioning.
Complex, rewarding technical challenges: Lead major high-voltage works and control systems integration within a live operating environment.
See the full project lifecycle: Follow your engineering decisions from design reviews through to energisation, performance testing and final handover.
A permanent career opportunity: Join an established Australian industry leader through a permanent appointment within its Capital Projects function.
An enviable regional lifestyle: Based in Marulan, enjoy the beautiful NSW Southern Highlands, known for its picturesque countryside, welcoming communities and access to Sydney and Canberra.

Ready to make your mark?

Major infrastructure projects require exceptional engineers, but truly successful projects need leaders who can bring technical expertise, commercial judgement and people together.

If you're ready to take ownership of a challenging electrical engineering programme and contribute to an investment that will shape the future of a major Australian operation, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Project Lead (Mechanical) Engineer, Marulan Infrastructure Upgrade
job.description:
Take ownership of the mechanical and structural engineering scope on a significant infrastructure upgrade within a live heavy industrial operation in Marulan.

This is a hands-on, site-based project leadership role for an experienced Mechanical Engineer who enjoys being close to the work: resolving technical issues, working with contractors and vendors, overseeing installation and ultimately taking mechanical systems through completion, commissioning and handover.

Working within an established capital projects team, you will lead the mechanical discipline across a major upgrade incorporating new crushing and bulk materials handling infrastructure within an operating site.

The opportunity
You will be the key point of accountability for the mechanical and structural scope, taking responsibility from design assurance and equipment procurement through construction, installation, completion and commissioning.

The project incorporates a new impact crusher, screening and conveying systems, stacker reclaimer and stockpile reclaim infrastructure, chute and transfer systems, structural steel, platework, piping and associated plant services. 

Importantly, this is not simply a design engineering position. You will spend significant time in the field working alongside contractors, operations, maintenance and other engineering disciplines to ensure the plant can be safely constructed, commissioned and integrated into an operating facility.

Key responsibilities
  • Own mechanical and structural design assurance across the project.
  • Lead technical review of equipment, drawings, specifications and vendor submissions.
  • Oversee crushing, screening, conveying and bulk materials handling packages.
  • Prepare technical specifications, scopes of work and tender evaluations.
  • Manage vendor technical performance and major equipment procurement.
  • Lead constructability and maintainability reviews with operations and maintenance.
  • Oversee mechanical and structural installation through the site delivery team.
  • Resolve contractor technical queries, NCRs, design changes and site issues.
  • Coordinate mechanical interfaces with civil, electrical and controls disciplines.
  • Manage mechanical interfaces with the operating plant, including shutdowns and tie-ins.
  • Own mechanical completions, punch lists and system turnover packages.
  • Support pre-commissioning, load testing, performance testing and final handover.
The position also has responsibility for a small mechanical team, with approximately 3 direct reports and 3-5 total reports plus contractor supervisory personnel. 

What we are looking for
You will be a practical Mechanical Engineer who has delivered major heavy industrial plant in the field and can comfortably move between engineering detail and construction delivery.  

Ideally, you will bring:
  • Degree qualification in Mechanical Engineering.
  • 10+ years' mechanical engineering experience within resources, quarrying, cement or heavy industrial capital projects.
  • Previous discipline lead or package leadership experience on significant capital projects.
  • Strong experience with crushing, screening, conveying or comparable bulk materials handling plant.
  • Working knowledge of conveyors, transfer points, chutes, structural steel and mechanical equipment.
  • Brownfield construction experience within a live production environment.
  • Experience taking equipment from design and procurement through installation and commissioning.
  • Strong contractor and vendor management capability.
  • Experience managing shutdowns, tie-ins and operational interfaces.
  • Sound mechanical completions and commissioning knowledge.
  • Experience with stacker reclaimers, enclosed stockpiles, cement, lime or quarry operations, offshore equipment sourcing and 3D model reviews will be particularly valuable. 
Why consider this role?
This is an opportunity to take genuine discipline ownership on a major, technically complex brownfield project rather than operating as one engineer within a large design team.

You will have visibility across the full project lifecycle and the ability to influence equipment selection, constructability, installation methodology, commissioning and operational handover.

The role is site based at Marulan for the project delivery phase, providing the opportunity to remain close to the construction and directly influence project outcomes.
